import.policy: verbatim import; narrow, story-documented deviations listed under 'deviations' — shipped 4.8.1 binaries outrank the published snapshot when they measurably disagree (PROJECT.md authority order)
import.verification: Files not named under 'deviations' must match upstream.sourceTree; deviating files are accounted for individually.

deviations.reason: SaveAs rooted-path guard (ledger P50)
request-cookie configured defaults; shipped 4.8.1 (System.Web 4.8.9319.0) carries a servicing fix absent from every published source branch, ported from IL readings

backmerged from upstream branch NetFramework48ZDP (e47d8c1b6482e0babe243dff2f9ece1507c814ff): SameSiteMode ConvertTo fix and cookieSameSite doc-comment corrections; the branch's comment-scrubber hunk in Util/AppSettings.cs was deliberately not taken
Dynamic Data enablement guarded behind a resolvable-type probe; System.Web.DynamicData is not carried (ledger P69)
case-folding the configuration system's mapped directory and composed web.config name on a case-sensitive filesystem (ledger P70)
the typed WebServices getter would recreate Framework's System.Web <-> System.Web.Services assembly cycle; it returns ConfigurationSection here (ADR-0009 amendment)
WorkItem.Post refused every non-Win32NT platform, a Win9x-era guard; the post lands on the ordinary thread pool, so the guard is fenced NETFRAMEWORK for one-way web methods off Windows

SetConfigurationFilePaths seam (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): the host publishes the machine/root config locations at bootstrap; the Framework fallback resolves against MsCorLibDirectory, which has no Config subdirectory on modern .NET, breaking consumers such as the WSDL help page path

the deserialization ctor chains to ClaimsPrincipal(SerializationInfo, StreamingContext), a throwing stub on modern .NET (SYSLIB0051); the base call is fenced NETFRAMEWORK and a payload guard refuses anything but a role-cookie ticket

AddIdentityAttachingRoles builds a DeferredRoleClaimsIdentity (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK) because ClaimsIdentity.ExternalClaims holds List<Claim> on modern .NET where Framework held IEnumerable<Claim>, so role claims cannot be parked unevaluated on a stock ClaimsIdentity

static responses opt out of server caching (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): IIS served them from its native module before any managed module could store one, so replaying them through the registered OutputCacheModule would defeat the revalidation the handler sets

the module collection is built from the merged system.webServer/modules snapshot through the integrated-mode builder already present here, with per-request managedHandler conditioning wrapped around the classic execution steps (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK), its answer settled once from the URL as it arrived and held on the context for the rest of the request, and the classic UrlMappingsExecutionStep retired in favour of the golden's UrlMappingsModule row

the golden registers this module in every application, so the anonymous WindowsIdentity/WindowsPrincipal statics move into a nested holder that defers their platform failure, and IsEnabled answers false (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK) rather than the authentication section's default, which is Windows

handler selection walks the merged system.webServer/handlers snapshot instead of the classic <httpHandlers> mapping (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): MapHttpHandler asks the walk for the handler and keeps the factory-recycling bookkeeping around it, and AssemblyResourceLoader asks the same list whether WebResource.axd is still mapped to it

IIS request filtering's <fileExtensions> deny list is checked beside the hidden-segment rule in ValidatePath (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK), because the retired classic <httpHandlers> table was what had been refusing those extensions

with the shipped classic <httpModules> table retired, InitModules publishes the merged module list through IntegratedModuleList, which only IIS's native wireup used to fill, and UrlAuthorizationModule.CheckUrlAccessForPrincipal reads it instead of scanning the classic section (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK)

RaiseRuntimeError writes the raised error to WebFormsRuntimeEventSource before the HealthMonitoringManager.Enabled gate, so request errors are delivered without healthMonitoring configuration; the gated body is unchanged and the addition is unfenced because Framework has no equivalent call
persisted autogen-key supplier and environment-supplied machineKey values behind NETFRAMEWORK fences (ledger P15)

classic Application_Start failure takes the integrated-mode contract behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: EnsureAppStartCalled latches context.Error into HttpRuntime.InitializationException and rethrows it on every later call, covering requests parked on the app-start lock and requests that reach it past the _appOnStartCalled fast path, and EnsureFirstRequestInit replays the latched exception on later requests, standing in for the FirstRequestInit gate and native-module replay that cover both cases under integrated IIS

the public integrated identity answers as an integrated IIS 10 pool behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences — UsingIntegratedPipeline returns true and IISVersion returns 10.0, the pair reading IV16 measured on the server whose applicationHost.config baseline the port ships — while the internal UseIntegratedPipeline stays false because it selects native notification plumbing; AppVerifier's SyncContextSendOrPostCalledBetweenNotifications assert therefore reads the internal flag, since the NotificationContext it demands is filled only by that plumbing

the integrated-only MapRequestHandler/LogRequest/PostLogRequest event family takes its integrated arm (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): the twelve sync and async accessor gates keep their PlatformNotSupportedException only under NETFRAMEWORK, ApplicationStepManager.BuildSteps adds the three CreateEventExecutionSteps calls with the Log pair inside the early-end jump target, HookupEventHandlersForApplicationAndModules rethrows a refused add_XXX instead of swallowing it off integrated, and HttpContext.RemapHandler asks the step manager (a second range predicate beside IsInBeginRequestStep) and raises Framework's Invoke_before_pipeline_event at or after the map step

the integrated shim batch takes its integrated arm behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: ApplicationStepManager records a notification boundary per CreateEventExecutionSteps call plus the handler-mapping and handler-execution steps and fills a per-step table from it, HttpApplication exposes TryGetCurrentNotification and raises the two pre-send events through RaiseSendResponseEvent, which reports SendResponse and restores HttpContext.Current; HttpContext.CurrentNotification and IsPostNotification read that table and otherwise raise the new Notification_outside_pipeline string added to System.Web.txt; HttpApplication.OnExecuteRequestStep and ThrowIfEventBindingDisallowed drop the UseIntegratedPipeline gate and close their window on _initInternalCompleted alone, because InitSpecial never runs here; HttpHeaderCollection.Add/Set/Remove gain a request arm whose server-variable mirror reads HttpRequest.ExistingServerVariables rather than the materializing getter, HttpRequest.EnsureHeaders and GetServerVars and HttpServerVarsCollection.Populate stop calling MakeReadOnly, and BuildUrl prefers a Host rewritten through the collection; HttpResponse.AddOnSendingHeaders drops its IIS7WorkerRequest test and WriteHeaders drains the subscription queue before generating headers; and HttpRequest.GetEntireRawContent and HttpBufferlessInputStream.ValidateRequestEntityLength no longer close the connection after an oversize body
